evidence: Receiving DO2 drops from 11.63 mg/L at t=50.0h to 6.47 mg/L at t=50.2h and remains ~6.2-7.0 mg/L through t=52.0h, diverging sharply from all three source batches (~10.8-11.5 mg/L at the same clock time).
Delayed product assay (t=48.0h sample, available 52.0h): P = 3.235 g/L, consistent with sources (2.98-3.06 g/L), indicating the production trajectory was healthy prior to the DO2 drop.
Constraint floor is 2.0 mg/L; current DO2 ~6.2 mg/L is above it, but the abrupt step change warrants a proactive oxygen-supply correction rather than continued KEEP.
increase_air action bound: aeration x1.15 with feed unchanged (allowed_actions), preserving product mass while restoring oxygen margin.
args.rationale: The receiving fermentation shows an abrupt, persistent DO2 collapse (11.6 -> ~6.2-7.0 mg/L) beginning at t=50.2h, diverging sharply from all source batches, while product formation (P = 3.24 g/L at t=48h sample) remains on track. The safest bounded intervention that restores oxygen margin without sacrificing product mass is to increase aeration by the allowed 15%. Feed reduction would retain DO2 at the cost of production; stop yields zero production; combined/strong reductions are unnecessarily aggressive given the large remaining margin above the 2.0 mg/L constraint. No extra assay was requested because the 4h-turnaround product assay would sample pre-drop material and add no actionable information.
args.uncertainty: The root cause of the DO2 step (hidden process fault vs. feed surge vs. kLa loss) is unobservable, so it is not certain that added aeration alone will restore DO2; if DO2 continues to decline after this intervention, a feed reduction would be the next escalation. The DO2 sensor could in principle be faulting, but the sustained multi-hour plateau at ~6.5 mg/L argues against a transient artifact. Assay clocks (4h assay delay, 12h sample-to-availability) limit real-time product visibility.
